title: Finance: Annuities and Loans
summary: Future value and present value annuities, sinking funds, loan repayments, outstanding balances, and analysing investment and loan options.

notes.text: An **annuity** is a series of equal payments made at regular intervals. In each formula, $x$ is the payment, $i$ the interest rate per period and $n$ the number of payments.

notes.caption: Future value: the amount saved by regular payments (e.g. a retirement annuity or sinking fund)
Present value: the value now of future payments (e.g. a loan or bond)

notes.title: Worked example 1: future value
notes.problem: Sipho saves R1 500 at the end of every month for 5 years at 8% p.a. compounded monthly. How much will he have?

notes.title: Worked example 2: loan repayment
notes.problem: A car loan of R200 000 is repaid in equal monthly instalments over 5 years at 11% p.a. compounded monthly, starting one month after the loan is granted. Find the instalment.

notes.text: The **outstanding balance** on a loan after some payments is the present value of the payments that remain.

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: Using worked example 2, what is the balance outstanding after 3 years (36 payments)?

notes.text: A **sinking fund** is a savings plan to replace an asset in the future. Find the future cost (allowing for inflation), subtract the scrap value of the old asset, and use the future value formula to find the monthly payment.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Decide first: is the money being **saved** for the future (future value) or **borrowed/withdrawn** now (present value)? Then make sure $n$ and $i$ use the same period (months with monthly payments).

notes.title: Worked example 4: how long?
notes.problem: How many monthly payments of R3 000 are needed to repay a loan of R100 000 at 12% p.a. compounded monthly?
steps: $n \approx 40{,}75$: 40 full payments and a smaller final payment.
